QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_2

question.text: A clearing member holds 10 long lots of 91-day T-Bill futures carried forward from yesterday. Yesterday's DSP was Rs. 97.80 and today's DSP is Rs. 97.50. Lot size is 2,000 units. What is today's MTM obligation?

answer.text: Pay Rs. 6,000 to the Clearing Corporation
Receive Rs. 6,000 from the Clearing Corporation
Pay Rs. 3,000 to the Clearing Corporation
Receive Rs. 12,000 from the Clearing Corporation

explanation.text: The Logic: For a long carried-forward position the daily MTM is (Current DSP - Previous DSP) x Lot Size x Lots = (97.50 - 97.80) x 2,000 x 10 = -0.30 x 20,000 = -Rs. 6,000. The negative sign means the long must pay Rs. 6,000 to the Clearing Corporation (option A). MTM uses the previous DSP as the base for carried-forward positions and the daily settlement price for valuation, per pp.107-113 and p.240 of the workbook. The Trap: Option B reverses the direction (this would be the short-side result). Option C halves the lot count. Option D doubles the price change. In the original ambiguous version the stem said only that the member "holds 10 lots" without specifying long or short, so a short position would receive Rs. 6,000 and option B would also be defensible. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the direction of the position was not stated. The stem has been tightened to "10 long lots" so that option A is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series IV (Interest Rates Derivatives, Dec 2025), pp.107-113, 240.
